mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (2) In any amount — and where there are many additional grounds for leniency, we rely on those who hold that chametz on Pesach is like other prohibitions in sixty [later authorities]:
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (4) Vessels in which it was cooked — even if one cooked much Israelite chametz in them on Pesach itself and it was absorbed, nevertheless after Pesach they are permitted, for then they are no longer ben yomo; and one does not transgress bal yeira'eh by keeping them, as in siman 451:
mishnah-berurah/1:כ: (11) Where it would be permitted — meaning, where we hold reicha is not significant b'dieved, the same applies to chametz; unlike where we are stringent in general, such as when the permitted food is davar charif:
mishnah-berurah/1:מ: (13) And specifically where — when the oven is small and sealed and chametz and matzah are uncovered inside, b'dieved reicha is not significant in general but l'chatchila forbidden (Yoreh De'ah 108); regarding chametz the latter view forbids even b'dieved. When reicha does not apply — large open oven or one covered — even in chametz one need not be stringent. Rama in Yoreh De'ah: in great loss rely on lenient view. Magen Avraham: only if small oven slightly open; if completely sealed no leniency even in loss. Hot food insulated for Shabbat (tsalent) — law like roasting, forbidden even in loss per Magen Avraham; most Acharonim lenient in loss or pressing need even in small sealed oven and in tsalent. Seal board should be new l'chatchila; b'dieved old board without rinsing does not forbid [Acharonim]:
mishnah-berurah/2:א: (14) That became mixed — if mixed intentionally when required with chametz, e.g. morayis with bread and sixty against bread — forbidden, must burn before Pesach; if Pesach passed some forbid benefit unless sold to gentile except value of prohibition:
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (15) From sixth hour — although lashed for eating and forbidden for benefit from Torah, ids no karet, Sages did not forbid in any amount; likewise noten ta'am lifgam. Chametz nokshah on Pesach — some forbid any amount; Magen Avraham and many hold no karet and only d'rabbanan — nullified in sixty even on Pesach, rely in pressing need. Last Yom Tov — forbidden by mixture like Pesach (467:10):
mishnah-berurah/2:ג: (16) Like other prohibitions — moist nullified in sixty; dry in dry one in two; eat before Pesach for it revives on Pesach (gloss seif 4):
mishnah-berurah/3:ד: (21) While wheat inside — if removed then heated, permitted; revival applies when substance present, here only flavor:
mishnah-berurah/3:ח: (25) On Pesach — although Yoreh De'ah 318 rules kli sheini does not discharge, on Pesach concern for stringent view:
mishnah-berurah/4:ה: (32) Moist in moist — beer in wine, flour in flour; see 453:17 — even unknown until Pesach, already nullified:
mishnah-berurah/4:ט: (36) Concern perhaps — taste nullified in sixty before Pesach; concern for crumbs at removal. Strain before Pesach — permitted; strain on Pesach does not help. Clear wine through fine strainer — ok; thick mead through coarse strainer — concern for crumbs:
mishnah-berurah/4:כ: (38) Imparts taste on Pesach — cold many permit (467:12) but here all forbid after twenty-four hours from fall [MA]. Bread in water on Pesach crumbles — forbidden unless strained before Pesach. Mead scum through flour strainer — nullified in sixty [Acharonim]:
mishnah-berurah/5:א: (39) Salted before Pesach — even chametz vessel; salting does not discharge; stam not ben yomo; lifgam permitted. Pickled twenty-four hours — lifgam even if ben yomo b'dieved:
mishnah-berurah/5:ע: (54) B'dieved no stringency — gloss stringencies l'chatchila only; if already cooked without rinse and cannot keep until after Pesach — permitted to eat; mixture not forbidden even in less than sixty. Garlic in butcher goods forbids mixtures; someSchool knife wiped some lenient in loss. Chopped garlic in salt for dry meat — permitted by soak and rinse if rinsed before Pesach; during Pesach only peeling [Eshel Avraham]:
mishnah-berurah/5:25: (63) And some lenient to drink mead all year; if concern fermented with beer yeast — forbidden; see 442:25; only where custom to ferment with yeast. If cooked in cauldrons used for burnt wine all year — forbidden. See 451:120 and Biur Halacha on charoset:
mishnah-berurah/5:27: (65) No stringency on mixtures — some hold vessel discharge is nat bar nat permitted before Pesach; stam not ben yomo; lifgam permitted — rely to not forbid mixtures; but if vessel known ben yomo from chametz absorption, Acharonim forbid mixtures as nat bar nat forbidden in chametz:
mishnah-berurah/5:36: (70) If placed before then — two months; Taz says thirty days; MA and Chayei Adam for drinking wine require two months:
mishnah-berurah/6:א: (78) Placed in mortar — even ben yomo if clean now; salt there long ago — pickling not in dry:
mishnah-berurah/7:א: (81) Unripe grapes pounded before Pesach — MB holds not charif; but Yoreh De'ah 96 — sour fruit is charif, so stringent; in our mortars mostly spices — minute taste nullified before Pesach even ben yomo [Acharonim]:
mishnah-berurah/7:ה: (85) During Pesach — before Pesach permitted by rinse; during Pesach stringent l'chatchila; MA — only regular gentile-cut fish; incidental cut of non-charif with chametz knife — rinse or scrape suffices:
mishnah-berurah/7:ו: (86) Chametz adhering — only non-charif; charif (and boser for us) — forbidden even if knife certainly clean before Pesach; only knife not used hot with chametz, e.g. scraping dough — permitted even on Pesach:
mishnah-berurah/8:ג: (91) According to all — per gloss seif 9 we are stringent on lifgam on Pesach unless removed chametz from vessel before erev night:
mishnah-berurah/9:א: (92) Dry in dry — slice of chametz in matzah slices not recognizable; loaf in loaves — davar shebeminyan not nullified even in thousand (Yoreh De'ah 110):
mishnah-berurah/9:ב: (93) Not nullified — since moist forbids any amount, also stringent dry; only if mixed erev Pesach until night — like other prohibions, dry nullified by majority; must eat all before night or revives (gloss 4). Some: first view only when prohibition from itself; if permitted item absorbed chametz — one in two even on Pesach; many disagree. Chametz vessel mixed with Pesach vessels — like dry not found use on Pesach; if mixed erev Pesach stringent not to use; if not ben yomo and Yom Tov joy prevented — lenient:
mishnah-berurah/9:ג: (94) Some say chametz on Pesach — only moist any amount; dry like other prohibitions one in two:
mishnah-berurah/10:א: (96) Lifgam permitted — although chametz any amount on Pesach, when taste spoiled prohibition gone; like Yoreh De'ah 103 for other prohibitions. For chametz itself see 442:9:
mishnah-berurah/10:ה: (100) Forbidden — for benefit selling to gentile may be lenient as also minute amount; Peri Megadim note 11 — last Yom Tov may lenient if both together even for consumption:
mishnah-berurah/11:ב: (102) Mixed before Pesach in sixty — permitted after Pesach even per those who forbid revival on Pesach; mixed in less than sixty and Pesach passed — forbidden; author holds transgression on mixture kezayit without sixty (442). Min b'mino — Torah majority nullifies, permitted after Pesach even one in two [MA]. Eshel Avraham end — consumption forbidden but benefit permitted. Acharonim — forbidden to mix l'chatchila before Pesach in sixty to eat on Pesach; permitted to mix to keep until after Pesach:
mishnah-berurah/11:ה: (105) Nullified in sixty — when moist or dry-moist, need sixty; dry in dry in all cases of author — even one in two permitted after Pesach. Third case after Pesach needing sixty is Tur; many Poskim disagree — after Pesach majority suffices; lenient in loss [Acharonim]:
mishnah-berurah/11:ו: (106) Redemption suffices — permitted even for consumption; only third case after Pesach; if before or during Pesach transgressed bal yeira'eh — after Pesach benefit only not eating. Dough leavened in beer yeast after Pesach — forbidden even benefit as davar ham'amid; in loss permit benefit by casting to sea and sell to gentile except dough without yeast. Wine with wheat/milk starch and sixty to clarify — permitted; no lifgam concern if nullified; not nullifying l'chatchila as intent is to fix wine:
mishnah-berurah/12:ב: (108) Lest it fall into food — b'dieved if fell and sixty against it — dispute if forbids any amount; see 1:14; keeping until after Pesach permitted according to all:
